comparisons.peer_topic: Redemption Price Mechanics for Various Preferred Stock Series
comparisons.peer_summary: The redemption price per share for Series A through F and Series Q through Y Preferred Stock is the liquidation preference plus declared and unpaid dividends, while the redemption price for Series O Preferred Stock is the liquidation preference plus accrued and unpaid dividends.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and GS disclose redemption mechanics that depend on dividend status (declared vs. accrued). MS specifies that Series A and C are redeemable at the redemption price plus accrued and unpaid dividends 'regardless of whether dividends are actually declared.' GS distinguishes between series, where Series A-F and Q-Y are redeemable at the liquidation preference plus 'declared and unpaid dividends,' while Series O is redeemable at the liquidation preference plus 'accrued and unpaid dividends.' The key difference is that MS applies the 'accrued regardless of declaration' standard to specific series, whereas GS applies the 'declared' standard to most series and only uses 'accrued' for Series O.

sentences.text: 3.Series A and C are redeemable at the redemption price plus accrued and unpaid dividends, regardless of whether dividends are actually declared, up to but excluding the date of redemption.

• The redemption price per share for Series A through F and Series Q through Y Preferred Stock is the liquidation preference plus declared and unpaid dividends. The redemption price per share for Series O Preferred Stock is the liquidation preference plus accrued and unpaid dividends.

comparisons.peer_summary: Each series of preferred stock has a liquidation value and redemption price of $10,000 per share plus accrued unpaid dividends. The aggregate liquidation value was $20.2 billion at December 31, 2024.
comparisons.comparison: Both MS and JPM disclose that their preferred stock redemption prices include accrued but unpaid dividends. MS states Series A and C are redeemable at the redemption price plus accrued and unpaid dividends. JPM states that each series of preferred stock has a redemption price per share of $10,000, plus accrued but unpaid dividends. While MS specifies the condition 'regardless of whether dividends are actually declared' for specific series, JPM's statement is general for all series, both resulting in the inclusion of accrued dividends in the redemption obligation.
